comparator.name: Dutch Language and Culture
comparator.academicYear: Coherent prospective 2027–2028 / 2028–2029 / 2029–2030 entry-cohort sequence, checked against adopted 2026–2027 OER
comparator.route: Nederlandse Taal en Cultuur, standard route without study abroad; first-listed literature thesis field
comparator.sourceNotes: A prospective entry-cohort sequence supplies twelve 5-EC compulsory courses in year one, six 5-EC core courses and 30 EC restricted choice of two Faculty of Arts minors in year two, and four 5-EC major courses, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC open free choice in year three. Total 60+60+60=180. The 2026–27 formally adopted programme-specific OER agrees on the first-year structure and most named second-year courses but lists LET-NTCB221 Psycholinguïstiek in both its concurrent B2 and B3 cohort tables. That single course is counted once in the prospective three-year entry-cohort route, not twice for credit. The later prospective third year contains Verdieping Moderne Nederlandse Letterkunde and Sociolinguïstiek in place of the current-cohort OER third-year list, and is explicitly provisional; it has not been represented as adopted 2026–27 regulation. The thesis is a required 10 EC independent research project; the first-listed Letterkunde thesis is a neutral formal instance among three allowed fields, without changing the programme identity. Zero-credit mentorship and RADAr do not enter the credit total. The optional abroad/educational-minor replacement route is not combined with the standard non-abroad year.

routeSelection.route: Nederlandse Taal en Cultuur, standard route without study abroad; first-listed literature thesis field
routeSelection.basis: The target is the generic Dutch Language and Culture bachelor. The ordinary non-abroad route retains a 30-EC minor choice and 30-EC open space, rather than imposing an optional foreign stay, teaching minor or Dutch specialist minor. A literary thesis is the first-listed allowed thesis field, not a claim that all students must choose literature. The prospective coherent cohort sequence avoids counting the same Psycholinguïstiek course twice across OER tables for different concurrent cohorts.

programmes.label: Dutch Language and Culture at Radboud University

exception.reason: Dutch language, Dutch and Flemish literary history, Dutch linguistics, and advanced academic analysis and writing in Dutch define this programme. Its compulsory courses include Dutch literature before and after 1800, history of the Dutch language, historical and modern Dutch literary study, first-language acquisition, speech sounds, syntax, sociolinguistics, psycholinguistics and a Dutch-field bachelor thesis. UCR has one basic Dutch-language course for everyday communication and genuine broader courses in literature, communication, rhetoric and psycholinguistics. Those broader subjects do not supply a sustained advanced Dutch-language or Dutch-literature sequence. A 24-course English-taught literature and communication degree would address some methods and themes but would change the named academic field and leave much of the Dutch core uncovered.
exception.curriculumContext: The present 2026–27 regulation has a duplicated second/third-year Psycholinguïstiek listing for concurrent cohorts. The prospective 2027–30 entry-cohort pages give a coherent 180-EC ordinary route, with future third-year content flagged as provisional. The exception concerns the absence of UCR Dutch-field depth, not an unresolved inability to account for 180 credits.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Read all 151 current enriched UCR course rows and their course descriptions, outline profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned terms. MCCCOMM112 Dutch is explicitly an introductory course in simple oral and written Dutch for everyday situations, not academic Dutch linguistics or literary history. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning analyse international or broadly Western literary texts; MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning, MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication and MCCCOMM311 Persuasive Communication cover stylistics and rhetoric; HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics examines language processing. These courses can support language-and-culture interests, yet none supplies Dutch historical literature, Dutch grammar and phonology, Dutch sociolinguistics or a Dutch-language capstone. A defensible 24-course closest-match Dutch degree cannot be scheduled from this catalogue.
